Jest picks up the files in `__mocks__` by itself when you call `jest.mock()`. Importing one by its path does not mock anything. The code under test still gets the real module, and your assertions look at a mock that nobody calls. Even with `jest.mock()`, the import by path is a second copy of the mock, not the one the code under test calls.

Import the real path and mock it. The test and the code under test then share the same mock.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";
import { sendEmail } from "./__mocks__/mailer";
import { register } from "./register";

test("sends a welcome email", () => {
  register("ada@example.com");
  expect(sendEmail).toHaveBeenCalled();
});
```

`require()` is checked too:

{/* bad */}
```js
const { sendEmail } = require("../__mocks__/mailer");
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, jest, test } from "@jest/globals";
import { sendEmail } from "./mailer";
import { register } from "./register";

jest.mock("./mailer");

test("sends a welcome email", () => {
  register("ada@example.com");
  expect(sendEmail).toHaveBeenCalled();
});
```
